title: The Cosmic Cliffs of Carina
explanation: The edge of the young, star-forming region NGC 3324 in the Carina Nebula, revealed in unprecedented infrared detail by the James Webb Space Telescope. What looks like a mountain range at twilight is the wall of a vast gaseous cavity, its tallest peaks some 58 light-years high.

title: Pillars of Creation — Webb
explanation: JWST's near-infrared portrait of the iconic Pillars of Creation in the Eagle Nebula (M16) — towering columns of cool gas and dust where new stars are being born.

title: Pillars of Creation — Hubble
explanation: Hubble's celebrated 2015 revisit of the Pillars of Creation, captured in visible light — a tableau that helped define a generation's image of the cosmos.

title: The Milky Way over Paranal
explanation: A sweeping panorama of our galaxy arching over ESO's Paranal Observatory, high in the Chilean Atacama Desert — one of the darkest skies on Earth.

title: A View from the Very Large Telescope
explanation: A deep look into the southern sky from ESO's Very Large Telescope in Chile.

title: Hubble Heritage
explanation: A classic from the Hubble Space Telescope's celebrated archive.

title: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week
explanation: A recent highlight from the ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week series.

title: A Little Red Dot in the Early Universe
explanation: James Webb peers across cosmic time at Abell 2744 — among the most distant objects ever studied.
